Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 08/23/2026
Patient: Adrian McLaughlin, 67-year-old male

Adrian McLaughlin presents today with complaints of back pain. Back pain began 08/18/2026 after bending to pick up a grandchild. He reports the pain is localized to the lower back and does not radiate. On examination, there is tenderness over the lumbar paraspinal muscles and some limitation in range of motion due to discomfort. Neurological examination is normal with no weakness or sensory changes noted. Vital signs are within normal limits. The assessment is acute musculoskeletal lower back pain. The plan includes conservative treatment with rest, use of NSAIDs as needed, and gentle stretching exercises. The patient is advised to monitor symptoms and return if pain worsens or if any neurological symptoms develop.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/19/2026
Patient: Adrian McLaughlin, 67-year-old male

MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/19/2026: acute osteoporotic T11 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging. Interval increase in T11 vertebral body height loss compared with radiographs from 08/22/2026.

Impression:
Acute osteoporotic compression fracture at T11 with bone marrow edema. There has been interval progression in vertebral body height loss since prior imaging.

notes.title: Spine Intervention Consultation
notes.author: Interventional radiologist
notes.text:
Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/21/2026
Patient: Adrian McLaughlin, 67-year-old male

History and Presentation:
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. On re-interview, the back pain began about six months ago, long before the 08/18/2026 episode of bending to pick up a grandchild; the earlier history was inaccurate. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture. Pain NRS 5/10 despite 4 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis. Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire score 21/24.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current pain management and brace use. Monitor symptoms and consider further intervention if pain or function worsens.
